# TODO.md — the persistent source of truth

This file is how work resumes after a context compaction, a restart, or a new
agent. Tick items as they finish. Add categories as plans land. If a task is not
here, add it and tick it. Implementation details do not belong here — only tasks
worth tracking.

Legend: `[ ]` pending · `[~]` in progress · `[x]` done · `[!]` blocked · `[-]` cancelled

### Icons (`@gpuixui/icons`)

`[x]` `[██████████]` 4/4

`[x]` Read a **stored icon name as the placeholder mark, not an empty box** —
`name` is a stored value as often as a literal (a saved toolbar, a workspace
layout, an action record), and `Icon` read `icons[name]` directly, so a name from
a release that renamed or dropped an icon answered `undefined` and `source` went
with it: measured in a window, the element kept its 24×24 box **and** its `Image`
accessibility node while painting nothing (two tints of the frame are
byte-identical), so an icon-only button read as its action and showed a blank
square. `iconMarkup` (`registry.ts`) takes the decoded value as `unknown` and
answers the new `help` mark — a glyph that reads as "unknown", with the caller's
`label` still naming the action — `isIconName` (`names.ts`) is the membership
guard, and `FALLBACK_ICON` names the placeholder; the set is 76 → **77** names.
Directions measured: with `icons[name]` restored, `registry.test.ts`'s stored-name
case, `Icon.test.ts`'s placeholder case, `docs.test.ts`'s stored-name case and the
window case `paints a mark for a stored name the set no longer carries` all fail
(`expected undefined to be '<svg …'`, `expected true to be false`), while the
green tree is 38/38 in the package and 9/9 in `runtime/icons.runtime.test.tsx`.
Docs: `docs/icon.mdx`'s API `name` row and description count, the package README's
new §Names and API exports, and the `COMPONENTS.md` Icons row. The set index
(`apps/docs/content/docs/primitives/index.mdx`, docs-site) prints the derived
count, so its one numeral moved with the set.

`[x]` Read a **stored size name as the default step, not a vanished box** —
`Icon`'s `size` and `Spinner`'s dot side both resolve through `iconPixels`, and
its name branch was a bare `ICON_SIZES[size]`: `size` is a stored preference as
often as a literal, so a name from a release that renamed or dropped a step
arrives as a string the union no longer names, and the lookup answered
`undefined`. `Icon` wrote that to `style.width`/`style.height`, and the runtime
paints a sized SVG with no side as a **full-width, zero-height** box — measured
in a window at **1256 × 0** inside a 1280px frame — so a toolbar row around a
vanished glyph stretched across the window. `iconPixels` now takes the decoded
value as `unknown` (the rule `revealFrames` follows) and reads a name the scale
does not carry as the `md` step, beside the numeric rule it already had;
`isIconSize` is the membership test, derived from `ICON_SIZES` rather than a
second list. `sizes.test.ts` gains `reads a name the scale does not carry as the
default step` and `runtime/icons.runtime.test.tsx`
`paints an icon whose stored size name the scale no longer carries`; directions
measured: with the bare lookup restored, the unit case fails

### Design tokens and theming (`tokens-theme`)

`[x]` `[██████████]` 267/267

`[x]` Read a **theme name a store wrote** as a name, not as a value to trim —
      `extendTheme` interpolated `overrides.name` and `styleName` trimmed the
      base's, so the stored route
      `restoreTheme(JSON.parse('{"mode":"dark","name":42}'))` returned a `Theme`
      whose `name` was the **number 42** (a field the type promises is a string),

The contract immediately found the documented brand: its dark primary `#6A45F0` carried a white label (5.6:1) but sat at 2.66:1–2.99:1 as a mark on the dark card, popover and muted strip, so the example and the house platform theme now own their on-colour **per mode** (dark `#B49CFF` with the near-black iris, light `#6A45F0` with white). `auditTheme` reports it as a seventh contract (`indicators`, counted in `passed`), so a brand is held to the same gate. `indicator.test.ts` (8 cases) holds the 16-theme sweep and its tightest placement (Luna light `success`/`muted` 3.30:1), the status rule, the unmeasurable case, a caller's stricter floor and the catalogue counts; `audit.test.ts` proves the gate fails on a mark no contrast pair can see; `platforms.test.ts` audits the house theme in both modes. Directions measured: removing a tone's mark role fails three cases (`warning/background`, `[ 'warning' ]`, and the printed count); `indicatorFailures` returning `[]` fails three; `passed` ignoring the report fails the gate case; and reverting the dark brand to `#6A45F0` fails the brand audit at 2.66:1. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Indicator marks, `docs/design-system.md` §8/§9, the package README and the `Indicator marks` inventory row

`[x]` Measure the numbers a theme carries — the audit checked every colour and **no number**, so a brand built from a scale factor or a stored preference could carry `NaN`/`Infinity` and ship. A style batch is serialised with `JSON.stringify` before it reaches native (`@gpuix/native@0.11.0`, `dist/mutations.js`), so those values arrive as `null` and the property is dropped: measured in the test renderer, `borderRadius: NaN` beside a valid `borderWidth`, `fontSize` and `backgroundColor` kept the three and dropped only the radius, and `fontSize: -4` was accepted and laid a text element out at height 0. `invalidNumbers(theme)` reports every numeric token that cannot be laid out (group, path, value, rule) — spacing, radius, border width, icon size, type size and leading, density metrics and every shadow number — with a rule that follows the design: a negative shadow offset or spread passes, a zero radius passes, a control height, icon or type size must be positive. `auditTheme` folds it into `passed` as its third report (eight now), and `numbers.test.ts` holds all 16 shipped, platform and authored themes to an empty report, proves each group with a broken value, proves both directions (removing the radius inspection fails 4 cases; dropping the field from `passed` fails 2; restored 14/14), reports a shadow's second entry behind a valid first, and executes `numbers.example.ts`. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Numbers/§Verification, `docs/design-system.md` §9–§11 and the package README; a `Token numbers` inventory row.

`[x]` Fold the **disabled fade** into the gate — `auditTheme` shipped eight reports while `disabledFadeFailures` (the mechanism `@gpuixui/tw`, the primitive cores and a menu row actually use) was not one of them, so a brand whose `primaryForeground` composites into its own faded fill passed the gate it is told to run. `ThemeAudit` gains `disabledFade` and `passed` reads it (nine reports now); the report deliberately keeps `contrastFloors.disabled` in every variant instead of inheriting `contrastFloorsFor(theme)`, because the fade cannot reach a high-contrast variant's 3:1 and folding the variant's floors in would fail every shipped high-contrast theme for a mechanism it does not use. `audit.test.ts` builds the brand that isolates it — `primary: "#101010"`, `primaryForeground: "#7E7E7E"` passes the enabled pair at 4.69:1 and lands at 1.04:1 when faded, with `contrast` and `indicators` both empty — and proves the fade report reads the same for a high-contrast theme at either floor set. `docs.test.ts` gains `the audit's report list`: every key `auditTheme` returns must be named in `docs/tokens.md`, the README and `docs/design-system.md`, no `audit.<name>` the gate does not return may be named, and the printed count word is derived from the gate's own keys. Five directions measured: dropping `disabledFade` from `passed` fails the erased-label case, returning `[]` fails it on the report, deleting the catalogue's line fails the name case (`docs/tokens.md: audit.disabledFade`), printing "eight" fails the count case, and planting `audit.nope` fails the stale case. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Checking your own theme and §The fade a disabled control paints, `docs/design-system.md` §8/§9/§11, the package README and the `Contrast contract` inventory row. The docs-site readout is the interlock row below.

`[x]` Measure the **state washes** — `hover`, `active`, `selected` and `accent` are the surfaces a control tints behind its content, and the contrast table measured only the *text on them*: a wash that carried the strip's own value was a colour the suite could not see. It was not hypothetical — the base dark theme shipped `hover` equal to `popover`, so hovering a menu row repainted the surface it already sat on; the base light theme's `hover` was its `muted` toolbar; macOS light's was its own muted strip; Windows light's and Linux dark's `hover` were within 1.05:1 of the strips they tint (measured 1.028 and 1.045). The washes join `decorativeSurfaces` as a sixth `stateWash` surface (four roles × `background`/`card`/`popover`/`muted`), held to the same `decorativeFloor` (1.05:1) the divider and skeleton use, so the existing `decorative` report and the audit gate cover them with no new API. Twenty-eight values moved in one change: the base light `hover` `#E4E9F0`, `accent`/`selected` `iris[100]`, the base dark `hover` `#272D37` and `active` `#333A46`, the macOS light/dark hovers, the Linux light/dark hovers and both accents, the Windows light hover/active/accent, the Luna and Aero light accents and Aero's light selected/active, the high-contrast dark accent/selected, and the house/Aero brand examples' accent families; all still clear every text pair and boundary. `decorative.test.ts` gains the 16-placement coverage case and a broken brand whose `hover` is its `muted` strip, and both directions were measured (removing the placements fails both cases; reverting dark `hover` fails the sweep naming `Dark`). Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Colour roles/§Decorative surfaces/§Verification, `docs/design-system.md` §8/§9, the package README and the `Contrast contract` inventory row.

`[x]` Measure the **filled action's resting surface** — `secondary` is the one filled variant with no brand colour and no border (`packages/primitives/src/core/variants.ts` paints `border: undefined`), so its fill is the whole button, and nothing measured it. It joins `decorativeSurfaces` as a seventh surface kind, `filledAction`, on the four strips a control can sit on (`background`/`card`/`popover`/`muted`) at `decorativeFloor` (1.05:1), so the existing `decorative` report and the audit gate cover it with no new API. **It found a shipped alias and nine style misses**: the base light theme shipped `secondary` as the `muted` value (`#EEF1F5`, 1.000:1), so a secondary button inside a muted toolbar was a label with no button around it; macOS light's window sat 1.015:1 from it, Linux light 1.040:1, Windows light 1.021:1, and the dark macOS/Windows/Luna/Aero palettes landed at 1.021–1.049:1 on their lighter popovers. The base light `secondary` is now `neutral[200]` `#E1E5EC` (one step above `muted`), its `active` wash `#D6DBE4` (so a resting control is not the value of a pressed ghost) and `borderStrong` `#75808F` (the new fill had taken the boundary pair to 2.95:1; it now clears 3.17 on `secondary` and 3.54 on `muted`), and each `darwin` set, all three dark sets and both authored looks own their control face. `decorative.test.ts` gains the four-placement coverage case and a broken brand whose `secondary` is its `muted`, both measured failing before the fix, and `decorative.example.ts` ships that brand as `flatActionBrand` so the documented call site reports the line; the shipped and platform sweeps fail when a face is reverted (measured: removing darwin dark's `secondary` fails `passes every platform style in both modes`; restoring light `secondary` fails three cases by name). Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Colour roles/§Action fills/§Decorative surfaces/§Platform styles/§Verification, `docs/design-system.md` §7/§8/§9, the package README, the platform chrome table and the `Contrast contract` inventory row. The `outline` variant's own edge is the interlock row below.

`[x]` Measure the **invalid state's edge** — validation failure swaps a control's border and its `focusVisible` line to `destructive` (`keyboardFocusRing(theme)` with the invalid colour in `packages/components/src/internal/theme.ts`, each primitive's `controlRing`), and every contract left it unmeasured on the surfaces it is painted on: `destructive` was a mark on the page, card, popover and `muted` strips, and the six strips a control sits on were covered by no pair at all for this role. Two pairs joined `contrastPairs` (55 → 57) — `destructive` on a field's own fill (`input`) and on a filled panel (`secondary`), the two strips the mark contract does not reach — both at `contrastFloors.boundary` (3:1; 4.5:1 high contrast), so the existing `contrast` report and the audit gate cover the edge with no new API. `[x]` Measure the dim the runtime paints on every other focusable — `keyboardFocusDim` is on by default, so pressing Tab fades every other control's fill and text, and nothing measured it because `contrastRatio` refuses a translucent result. `keyboardFocusDimOpacity` records the share (`0.4`) measured from the `keyboard-focus-dim` window capture, not assumed: the dark `muted` fill `#222730` paints `#181C23` and the `foreground` text `#EEF1F5` paints `#6E7177` over that fill — both `blend(colour, behind, 1 - 0.4)`, and the text over the *dimmed fill* rather than the page, so the disabled fade's composite is the shared rule (`src/fade.ts`). `keyboardDimPairs` names the 32 placements (three filled actions, a field and its placeholder, a focusable row's own text, a selected row, on the four strips) and `keyboardDimFailures(theme, floor?)` measures them at `decorativeFloor` — the dim is a where-can-Tab-go cue, not a reading mode: the tightest shipped placement is Linux light's `primary` over a card at 1.27:1, which is the measured reason a control whose text must stay readable opts out with `keyboardFocusDim: false`. `focus-dim.test.ts` (9 cases) holds the capture values, all 16 shipped/platform/high-contrast/look themes, the erased label, the unmeasurable role and a caller's stricter floor; `design-system-docs.test.ts` holds the page to the exports. `[x]` Give **brand-coloured text** a measured colour — a link, a text action and a breadcrumb's current page are written in `primary`, which is a **fill** designed to carry `primaryForeground`: no contract measured the role as text (only the mark contract reads it, at the 3:1 a bar or dot needs), so a link passed every suite while unreadable. Measured, the fill role is under the 4.5:1 text floor on the eight surfaces a link can sit on in most styles — the base light brand **4.30:1** on the `active` wash a pressed link tints behind itself, macOS dark **3.10:1** on `active` (3.81:1 on its popover), Linux light 3.44:1, Luna light 3.53:1, Aero light 3.83:1, and Windows XP's page 4.31:1. `brandText(theme, floors?)` returns the theme's own `primary` where it already reads (base dark, high-contrast light, Linux/Windows/Aero dark) and otherwise moves it toward the theme's `foreground` in 2% steps until the worst of `brandTextSurfaces` (background, card, popover, muted, plus the `hover` and `active` washes) clears `contrastFloorsFor(theme).secondary` — 4.5:1 default, 7:1 high contrast, so the high-contrast dark brand's 6.94:1 steps once. It stops at `foreground` and returns an unmeasurable brand unchanged rather than inventing a colour. `brand-text.test.ts` (17 cases) holds the premise by name, all 16 shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored themes on all eight surfaces (the two row washes joined them — see the row above), opaque output, minimality, the channel move, the variant floor, a pale brand, an unpaintable and a translucent brand, the foreground cap and the executed example; both directions measured (returning the raw brand fails 6 cases, jumping to `foreground` fails 3). `[x]` Hold a **theme's control heights** to the pressable floor — `targetSize` fixes 24px and `target.test.ts` held every *shipped preset* to it, but the gate a brand is told to run only asked for `> 0`: `extendTheme(lightTheme, { density: { controlHeight: { sm: 20 } } })` passed every report while every control built at that height — the library reserves no hit-area padding on top of `controlHeight` — became a target WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 says a reader cannot reliably hit, and `docs/design-system.md` §6's claim ("a control built at a control height never needs extra hit-area padding") became false in silence. `NumberRule` gains `pressable` (finite, `>= targetSize.minimum`) and the `controlHeight` group is inspected with it, so the report — and `auditTheme.passed`, which already reads it — names the size: `numbers.test.ts` proves a 20px height reports `{group: "density", path: "controlHeight.sm", value: 20, rule: "pressable"}`, that the floor itself passes (which is why `compact` `sm` at exactly 24 still ships), that only the sizes a shrunken density puts under it are reported, and that a brand whose only defect is a 20px height fails the gate with every colour report empty. No palette or metric moved. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Numbers/§Target sizes, `docs/design-system.md` §6, the package README and the `Token numbers`/`Target sizes` rows; `design-system-docs.test.ts` fails if the page drops the rule. Three directions measured: reverting the rule to `positive` fails four cases by name, deleting the page's sentence fails the docs guard, and a `radius.lg` below `radius.md` fails the new shipped-scale ordering case. Same commit adds the missing hierarchy guards for the shipped **radius, border and icon** scales — `scale.test.ts` only ordered spacing, density and avatars, so an inverted radius or icon step could ship.

`[x]` Measure a **bordered control's edge on the wash it tints** — `borderStrong` was held to 3:1 on the surfaces a control *rests* on, and the second action changes its fill the moment a pointer arrives: `packages/components/src/internal/button.tsx`'s `secondary` variant paints `borderColor: borderStrong`, then hands the same element to `hover`/`active` as its background, so its edge sits on the wash — a strip no pair measured. Two pairs joined `contrastPairs` (57 → 59) at `contrastFloors.boundary`, and they found four shipped misses: the base light theme's pressed secondary at **2.88:1**, the base dark theme's at **2.86:1**, high-contrast dark at **4.15:1** against its own 4.5 floor (the default floors called it a pass), and Linux light at **2.96:1** hovered and **2.77:1** pressed. The four `borderStrong` values moved the least distance that clears every strip — `#727D8C` (was `#75808F`), `#788494` (`#748091`), `#A7A7A7` (`#A0A0A0`) and Linux light's `#7E7C79` (`#84827E`) — and every pair they already carried still clears its floor (the tightest is the base light edge on `active` at 3.01:1). `contrast.test.ts`'s boundary suite now requires `hover` and `active` in its coverage, reports both pre-fix values by name (`2.88` at the default floor, `4.15` at the high-contrast one), and reports a brand whose edge equals its own wash at 1.00:1; `color.test.ts` and `platforms.test.ts` enumerate the pair table per theme, so reverting a value fails by name (`light: borderStrong on active meets 3:1`, `linux light: borderStrong on active meets 3:1`) and the audit sweep fails too — measured both ways. `catalogue-values.test.ts` named the four stale printed cells before the pages moved. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Contrast/§Action fills, `docs/design-system.md` §7/§9 and the `Contrast contract` row.

`[x]` Decide what carries a **field** — `docs/design-system.md` §7 claimed `borderStrong` is the boundary "input and control boundaries" draw while both shipped painters rest on the decorative `border` role, and §8 plus `docs/tokens.md` still said the primitives' field recipe paints a destructive **fill** behind the value, which stopped when `FIELD_INVALID` became `aria-invalid:border-destructive` (`c193954e`). **Decision: the edge carries a field, not its fill** — a field sits on the page, a card, a popover and a `muted` toolbar, and in the light palettes the page (`#F6F8FA`) and a card (`#FFFFFF`) are only 1.06:1 apart, less than the perceptibility floor applied twice, so no fill can be seen against both (light `input` is `#FFFFFF`, the same value as `card` and `popover`). Both pages now state the rule, the measured reason and the shipped deviation (`fieldVariant` and `FieldInput` paint `border`, 1.19:1 on the light page, and reach `borderStrong` only on hover), and retract the destructive-fill claim. `field-boundary.test.ts` (5 cases) reads the two painters: adopting `borderStrong` fails until §7's deviation sentence moves, restoring `aria-invalid:bg-destructive` fails by name, a page that stops naming the file it describes fails, and each printed ratio (1.06, 1.00, 1.19, 1.26, 3.31) is held to `contrastRatio`. Four directions measured — deleting the deviation sentence, adopting `borderStrong` in both painters, restoring the invalid fill, and changing the printed resting-edge ratio each fail the named case. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Contrast/§The invalid state/§Limitations and `docs/design-system.md` §7/§8. Adoption is the interlock row below

`[x]` Hold a **type role's leading to its own size** — `invalidNumbers` checked that a type size and a leading were finite and positive, and never that the two numbers meant anything together: a type scale computed from a factor (`lineHeight: size * 0.7`) keeps every value finite and positive while the next baseline starts inside this line's glyph box, so consecutive lines collide and every suite stayed green. `NumberRule` gains `leading` — the one rule about two tokens, applied where the pair sits together in `inspectType`, so a zero or non-finite leading is still reported once as `positive` rather than twice — and `auditTheme.passed` reads it through the existing `invalidNumbers` report, so no gate shape, count or docs-site readout changed. `numbers.test.ts` (28 cases) proves the report by name, accepts a leading exactly equal to the size (lines touch, they do not overlap), proves the single-report rule for an unusable leading, holds every shipped role above the floor, and executes the new `crushedTypeTheme`/`crushedTypeAudit` in `numbers.example.ts`. Four directions measured: dropping the comparison fails 4 cases by name, a shipped `body` leading of 12 fails the 16-theme sweep and the scale case, a catalogue row that drops the rule fails the docs case, and a design-system sentence without it fails the prose case. `[x]` Decide the **faded control on a card** — `disabledFadePairs` holds the three filled actions on the page and a field on `background`/`card`/`popover`, and a fade's composite depends on the strip its fill is faded over. `[x]` Hold a **declared switch's box** to the numbers it is drawn with — the

`height: 0` or `knob: -2` and `auditTheme` passed: the batch drops a `NaN` so the

`switchMetricSlots` and `switchMetricFailures(theme)` are the contract —
`audit.switch.metrics`, so the gate fails a box it cannot draw — and it holds the
two relations the primitive's travel relies on: the track's height contains the
knob plus both insets, and its width contains the same plus a pixel of travel
(the inset includes the edge, which is why Fluent's 12 at 4 is exactly its 20).
**It found the proportional scale's own arithmetic**: `switchMetricsAt` rounded

No native scenario applies — an example's call site and the timer it hands over.

The `markdown-fence` live probe mounts three fences from one four-line `ts` source on 0.11.0: the base dark page paints body `#191C22` (**174 776** px) and strip `#1E2126` (**57 822** px) with keyword `#A7A9FF` (**896** px); the macOS dark page paints `#242426` (**174 570**), `#28282A` (**57 630**) and `#B0B2FF` (**896**); and a host handed no theme paints the runtime's `#8F96ED` (**988**). Both derived composites landed where the seam says, the strip is a second wash (1.057:1 base, 1.053:1 platform) carried by the runtime's rule rather than a boundary, and each keyword clears the body floor on its own fence. **The measured rule: a fence composites over the fill *behind* the host, not over the theme object's `bg`** — the first run mounted the platform block on the shell's base-dark page and its fence painted `#191C22`, with the expected `#242426` on **6** rounded-corner pixels, so the view paints each block on its own theme's page. 50 checks, `--only markdown-fence`, green (~0.6 s, stable across three runs; the body counts move by a few hundred glyph-edge pixels). Fixture `src/live/markdown-fence.ts` + `markdown-fence.test.ts` (14 cases: both washes from the seam, both keywords from `syntaxColors`, a brand that clears the page at 7.17:1 and misses the fence at 6.63:1, the source's one fenced block, the page-wrapper wiring, the registry, the count and the measured inks). Negative control measured, exit `1`, restored green: painting the platform block on the shell's page fails `the platform fence paints its own body fill`. Evidence: `apps/playground/README.md` §`markdown-fence`, `.artifacts/live/markdown-fence.png`. The catalogue and capability record that should cite it are the Interlocks row **Publish the fence a window paints**

`[x]` Measure **whether a fade removes the hitbox or only the ink** — every leaving surface fades to `opacity: 0` and stays mounted for its exit, and both `presenceStyle`'s `pointerEvents: "none"` and `PresenceShield` rest on a question `opacity-paint` did not ask: does the box still take input? The `faded-hitbox-lifecycle` live probe mounts a control at zero, a painted target under a transparent cover, and the same pair with an inert cover, and measures on 0.11.0: the faded control still reports its **200×32** box, paints the page at its centre, keeps its **Tab stop**, hears a press (`faded=1`) and a key typed while focused (`keys=1`); the transparent cover paints the target's fill through it yet takes the press itself (`cover=1 target=0`); and `pointerEvents: "none"` lets the press reach the target (`inertTarget=1`) **while the cover's own handler still runs** (`inertCover=1`) — the opt-out removes the hitbox, not the handler, so a shield must be a surface with no action of its own. 19 checks, `--only faded-hitbox-lifecycle`, green on 0.11.0 here (~0.7–1.5 s). Fixture `src/live/opacity-hit.ts` + `opacity-hit.test.ts` (9 cases: the locators and press cases, the share and box, the readout, the check count, the registry entry, the printed checks and reads, the three rules and the negative control, and the view's wiring). Negative control measured, exit `1`, restored green: making the second pair non-inert (`inert={false}`) fails `the inert cover lets the press through to its target` (`inertCover=1 inertTarget=0`). Evidence: `apps/playground/README.md` §`faded-hitbox-lifecycle`, `.artifacts/live/faded-hitbox{,-pressed}.png`. The motion seam's guard and the shield now cite a measured rule rather than an inference

      `hidden-subtree-lifecycle` probe mounts both around a focusable control and
      the shipped `Carousel` on 0.11.0: the `display: none` control still reports
      its own **200×32** box, paints its `#1E222A` fill on the `#11141A` page and
      keeps its Tab stop, while the `visibility: hidden` control reports **no**
      box, leaves its 32-point row painting the page and is **skipped** by the
      traversal. It measured the carousel **painting both slides** in one row,
      each **433** wide, before and after a step — the defect its owner then
      fixed by mounting only the slide on screen — and the probe now asserts the
      fixed shape: one slide box **866** wide inside the **868** carousel, no
      spare-slide stop in the walk, and after a step the first frame unmounted
      with the second the only box painted. A code focus on the invisible control
      reports its id but a typed key never reaches it (`invisibleKeys=0`).
      24 checks, `--only hidden-subtree-lifecycle`, green on 0.11.0 here
      (~1.2 s). Fixture `src/live/hidden-subtree.ts` + 15 unit
      cases (the two words and their costs, the stops the window measured, the
      readout, the count, the registry entry, the README's printed reads, rules
      and negative control, and the view's wiring); view and steps in
      `src/live/hidden-subtree-probe.tsx`. One negative control measured, exit
      `1`, restored green: painting the `display: none` control in the page role
      fails `the display:none control paints its own fill` (`expected false, got
      true`), so the paint read compares frame bytes rather than the style's
      intent. **The probe found a component defect** — the shipped `Carousel`

      (300/200 where the rule needs an over-full row) and the headless

      split it evenly (**140/140**), an auto basis grows from content (**70/210**),
      **a grower whose content is wider than its share keeps its content and the
      other takes the rest (200/80, not 140/140)** — so `flex-1` is not equality
      and a truncating column declares `minWidth: 0` — an over-full row shrinks the
      item that may shrink (**180**) while `flexShrink: 0` keeps **320** painted
      past the row, an item's automatic minimum is its content (**300** in a 200
      row) until `minWidth: 0` lifts it (**200**), `maxWidth` stops a grower
      (**120**, row left short), and `alignSelf` places content width at

      layout-flex-sizing` green in the full **45/45** suite. Fixture
      `src/live/flex-sizing.ts` + `flex-sizing.test.ts` (12 cases: the arithmetic,

`[x]` Measure **whether a roving-focus widget holds in a window** — Tier 4's
      *Keyboard navigation* row was `?`: a data grid, tree or toolbar is one tab
      stop whose arrows move real focus, and the runtime's focus handles were
      verified while the model was the caller's. The `grid-focus-lifecycle` live
      probe mounts a 3×3 grid whose remembered cell carries `tabIndex: 0` and
      the other eight `-1`, with a focusable control either side: Tab enters at
      the remembered cell, `Right`/`Down`/`Home`/`End`/`Up` each move real focus
      and the remembered cell follows (`roving=r0c1`), an arrow at an edge
      **clamps** rather than wrapping, Tab leaves after one press, a press on
      `r2c1` activates it and becomes the remembered cell (`activations=1`),
      Tab re-enters there, `focusElement` reaches a `-1` cell, and `Shift+Tab`
      leaves backwards. **The measured caveat:** `tabIndex: -1` is a sort key,
      not an exclusion — the runtime orders a negative cell **before** the
      zero-index stops, so Tab from a programmatically focused `-1` cell
      (`gridfocus-r2c2`) lands on `grid-focus-before`, not after the grid; the
      model holds while focus only moves through the app's arrows, and a
      component that focuses a non-roving cell must expect that exit. 20 checks,
      `--only grid-focus-lifecycle`, green on 0.11.0 (~1 s). Fixture
      `src/live/grid-focus.ts` (the 3×3 geometry, `moveIndex`/`tabIndexOf`,
      `gridKeyOf`, the readout, `GRID_FOCUS_CHECKS`) + `grid-focus.test.ts` (14
      cases: the geometry, both axes, every clamp, `Home`/`End`, the key filter,
      the one-zero rule, the tab-stop list, the readout, the registry entry, the
      view wiring, this section and the printed count). Two negative controls
      measured, exit `1` each, restored green: making every cell `tabIndex: 0`
      fails `Tab leaves the grid after one press` (`expected
      "grid-focus-after", got "gridfocus-r1c0"`), and wrapping `Right` fails

`[x]` Measure a **scroll region's keyboard contract through a window's delivery

      window has no such verb: a key reaches the focused element and bubbles, and
      the viewport's handler stands down unless `getFocusedElementId()` is its own
      id, so the **traversal** that reaches the stop is part of the contract. The
      `keyboard-scroll-lifecycle` live probe mounts a 200×160 vertical region (a
      40px field slot and eleven 40px rows, end `-320`) beside a 320×120 sideways
      one (eighteen 80px columns, end `-1120`) and drove them on 0.11.0: a

      `pagedown` moves one viewport (`-192` from `-32`); a third page clamps at
      `-320` rather than asking for `-480`; `end` reaches the content's end and
      `up`/`pageup` never pass the origin; `cmd-home` moves nothing; a press in
      the field inside the region starts the text session (`ab` reaches
      `onChange`) and its arrow leaves the region still; the sideways region pages
      by the width it shows (`-352`), reaches `-1120`, and a vertical key leaves
      it still; a `focusable={false}` region is skipped by the traversal and
      answers no key. 62 checks, `--only keyboard-scroll-lifecycle`, green on
      0.11.0 (~1.4 s). Fixture `src/live/keyboard-scroll.ts` (`predictedOffset`,
      both geometries, one readout spelling) + `keyboard-scroll.test.ts` (7 cases).
      Three directions measured, exit `1` each, restored green: pinning the page
      step to one line fails `pagedown moves kscroll-vertical`
      (`expected -64 ± 1, got -192`), dropping `focusable={false}` fails `a

      "kscroll-inert"`), and the fixture's clamp prediction at `-480` fails

      runtime suite. A window is a different delivery path, and

      shipped `Button` four times (enabled, `disabled`, `loading`, a second

      point (the painted box's centre, ±1); Enter activates on its **press** and

`[x]` Measure **which handler a press on a composite row's inner element runs** —
      the rule every Tier 3 row composes against (a checkbox cell, a sort arrow,
      a trailing menu) and Tier 4's tree rows reuse, and the repo's only answer
      was a comment in `carousel.tsx` claiming the runtime runs the innermost
      handler alone. The measured rule is about **painted surfaces**: GPUI's
      `hit_test` stops counting an element as hovered at the first
      `BlockMouseExceptScroll` hitbox, which `packages/native` inserts for a

      and the prepended rows are retained while unpainted, so "nothing moved"
      is a real splice. A second 2-row list is the control: short content
      re-anchors to row 0 on every layout, so it reads the same with the anchor
      broken. 21 checks, `--only virtual-list-prepend`, green on 0.11.0; full
      headless suite re-run 39/39. Three negative controls measured (the feed
      starting at 4 rows: `the feed's declared rows overflow the viewport`, and
      with that guard relaxed `the wheel moved the feed off the top`; a
      `scrollTo` to the top inside the prepend handler, the naive "show the
      newest page": `the new rows stay above the viewport`; `followTail` on the
      feed: `the feed starts at its first row` — `expected 100, got 104`; exit
      `1` each, restored green). Evidence: `apps/playground/README.md` §A
      prepended page

`[x]` Measure the **loading-row correction** for infinite scroll — when the row
      standing in for the arriving page *is* the anchor, a page spliced beside
      it replaces the screen the reader was reading; the app owns the restore,
      and the append twin rests on the at-end sentinel instead. The live probe
      `loading-row-correction` mounts four identical lists (80px void, 40px
      rows, 160px viewport): a naive and a corrected pair at each edge. Measured
      on 0.11.0 — prepend: the void is the anchor (`itemIndex 0`), the naive
      splice paints the page's first row at the exact pixel the reader's message
      held (`y=80`) and the message leaves the screen, while the corrected list
      keeps the message at `80`, fills `0..80` with the page and asks
      `scrollToItem(3, -80)`; a second page with a message anchor is left alone
      (`guarded=1`, message still `80`, new page above). Append: a bottom list
      at its end reports the at-end sentinel (`itemIndex == 11`), the naive
      splice follows it to `14` and paints the page at `y=0` with the reader's
      message gone, while the corrected list pins the page's first row on the
      void's old top edge (`y=80`), keeps the row above at `40`, asks
      `scrollToItem(10, -80)`, and fires again after a wheel back to the end
      (`scrollToItem(12, -80)`). 58 checks, `--only loading-row-correction`,
      green on 0.11.0. The rule is native-free in `src/live/loading-row.ts` with
      `loading-row.test.ts` (8 tests) holding its arithmetic. Three negative
      controls measured: offset `0` instead of the rule's →
      `the corrected load leaves the reader's message where it was — expected 80
      ± 1, got 0`; removing the prepend guard →
      `the reader's message still painted — expected a value, got none` (the app
      moved the reader twice); the unit-level wrong index →
      `Some({index: 1})` against `Some({index: 3})` — exit `1` each. Two
      mechanics the probe settled: `scrollToItem` must be queued **after** the
      splice (a call beside `setPage` applied against the old child list, and
      the splice then shifted it again: the message landed at `y=0`), so the
      probe wraps the commit in `@gpuix/react`'s `flushSync`; and
      `getListScrollTop` names the **row at the viewport top after layout**, not
      the request, so the probe records the request in its readout
      (`request=3:-80`) and proves the pixel from `bounds`. Evidence:
      `apps/playground/README.md` §`loading-row-correction`,
      `.artifacts/live/loading-row-corrected.png`

`[x]` Land the `a11y-tree` headless scenario and measure **what assistive
      technology is told** — the library documents `aria-description`, an
      `aria-selected` row, a dialog role and a roving tree, and nothing had ever

      `Button`, `option` → `ListBoxOption`, `heading` → `Heading`,
      `progressbar` → `ProgressIndicator`); `aria-label`/`aria-description`/
      `aria-id` reach `label`/`description`/`author_id`;
      `aria-selected`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-level`/`aria-valuetext` reach
      `selected`/`expanded`/`level`/`value`; `onClick`+`tabIndex` surface as the

      **a node needs a role to exist at all** — a div carrying only an
      `aria-label` paints no node and `role="none"` is dropped. 19 checks,

      describes "Save project" — expected a value, got none`; dropping its

      the file", got ""`, exit `1` each). Evidence:

`[x]` Land the `dock-reflow` headless scenario and measure **the re-clamp signal

      bounds", via `onLayout`) had never been measured: an `onLayout` that fired
      only for the first paint would make the workaround useless. A 560px row of
      a 120px sidebar, a flexible centre and a fixed 100px inspector; `Widen

      layout pass arrives **before** the new width applies and reports the box

      the next frame and equals the pane's painted `bounds`; the 100px inspector
      keeps its box and **still receives a report** (its count reaches 2); and
      narrowing reports the original 340 again. So the signal exists, but a
      report is not a "you changed" event — a stale pass arrives first and an
      unchanged pane is reported to — so a re-clamp acts on the width the payload
      carries and is idempotent. 12 checks, `--only dock-reflow`, green on
      0.11.0 (the counts behind it re-run three times); full headless suite
      re-run 37/37. Two negative controls measured (a centre that does not flex:

`[x]` `packages/primitives`: the **two sliders were the last focusable controls with no address or announced help** — the pass that gave `Input`/`TextArea`, `NumberField`, `OTPField`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Toggle`, `RadioGroup` and `Rating` a `ref`/`aria-id`/`onLayout` and `description` → `aria-description` skipped `Slider` and `RangeSlider`, so a form could not focus the slider it failed on, an automation host could not address it, and a visible `Label`'s help line reached nobody (no `aria-describedby` exists in 0.11.0). `Slider` carries all four on its root — both the slider and its tab stop — and `RangeSlider` announces the help on the group node while the address lands on the thumb a form should focus (the one holding keyboard focus, else the start), because only one element can hold it. The docs also said the slider's keyboard ring was painted on the thumb while the code declares it on the track; the page now says the track. Proof: `Slider.test.tsx`'s `hands its element the caller's address, layout and help` (the merged ref keeps the track registration), its blank-description case, and `addresses the thumb the form focuses and announces the group's help`; `runtime/address.runtime.test.tsx` adds both controls to its window and reads the help, the author id and the ref back off the runtime's own elements. Directions measured: reverting `Slider.tsx` fails both unit cases and all three native cases (`expected undefined to be 'Controls the output level.'`, `'volume-track'`, `44`), restored 776 unit / 226 runtime green.
`[x]` `packages/primitives`: the **last two focusable controls without an address or announced help were the group controls** — `CheckboxGroup` and `ToggleGroup` are composite controls a form owns, but neither took `description`, `ref`, `aria-id` or `onLayout`, so a form could not focus the group it failed on, an automation host could not address it, and a visible `Label`'s help line reached nobody (0.11.0 has no `aria-describedby`). Both now announce `description` on the group node and put the address on the row/option that holds the tab stop — the only focusable element — while the wrapper stays unfocusable, the same rule `RadioGroup` and `Rating` already follow. The caller's ref is composed with the roving registration, so a keyboard move still paints its ring. Proof: `CheckboxGroup.test.tsx` and `ToggleGroup.test.tsx` gain `announces the group's help and addresses the row that holds the stop` (help, the addressed row, the merged ref, the neighbours left unaddressed); `runtime/address.runtime.test.tsx` mounts both groups and reads the help, the author id and the ref off the runtime's own elements. Directions measured: reverting the two components fails both unit cases and all three native cases (`expected undefined to be 'Pick at least one.'`, `'channels-row'`, `34`), restored 778 unit / 226 runtime green.
`[x]` `packages/primitives`: a **non-finite `NumberField` value crashed the field** — the draft decided whether its owner's value had moved with `===`, and `NaN` never equals itself, so `NumberField value={NaN}` folded the draft on every render, called `setDraft` each pass and React stopped the field with "Too many re-renders" (measured: the offscreen renderer threw it before the first paint; `Math.min`/`Math.max` also passed `NaN` through, so the text, the bounds and both steppers agreed on `NaN`). The comparison is `Object.is` (`NaN` has not moved), and `core/number.ts` is now total the way `core/value.ts` already was: a value it cannot lay out reads as the nearest bound (`min`, else `max`, else 0), a bound that is not a number is not a bound, a non-finite step reads as one, and a step starts from the clamped value the field paints. `numberFieldPart.current` and the display text both read the clamped value, so the arrows step from what is on screen. Proof: `core/number.test.ts` gains the clamp, bounds, step-base and non-finite-step cases plus `syncNumberDraft`'s `does not fold a value that never equals itself` (all six measured failing at HEAD), `NumberField.test.tsx` gains `reads a value it cannot paint as the bound it can`, and `runtime/number-field.runtime.test.tsx` mounts `value={NaN}` with `min={0}` and reads `0` off the a11y tree with an `up` arrow reporting `1` (measured failing at HEAD with the re-render loop; 14/14 green with the fix). Docs in `docs/number-field.mdx` §Limitations/§Verification and the `COMPONENTS.md` Number Field row.
`[x]` `packages/primitives`: the **fixed-decimal text had two lies** — `formatNumber` promises "fixed decimals, never a thousands separator", while `(-0.004).toFixed(2)` is `-0.00`, so a field with `precision={2}` painted a negative number that means zero (the components package dropped the same sign from `SlidingNumber` in `eb3afa31`), and `toFixed` switches to the exponential form at `1e21`, so a value the parser accepts as text (`1e21`) committed as `1e+21`. `formatNumber` now drops a sign that belongs to the rounding rather than to the value, and expands the exponential form into the plain integer it means (every double that large is an integer) with the requested decimals. `core/number.test.ts` gains `does not sign a value that rounds to zero` and `keeps its fixed decimals past the exponential bound`, both measured failing at HEAD (`expected '-0.00' to be '0.00'`, `expected '1e+21' to be '1000000000000000000000'`); docs in `docs/number-field.mdx` §API/§Verification.

`[x]` `packages/components`: the shipped `ImageZoom` can report a **leave while the pointer rests inside its frame** — the playground's `image-zoom-lifecycle` failed twice under a loaded box (five agents building at once) and passed on a quiet one, with the same direction each time: an extra leave arrives between the two moves that hover one point, so the picture drops back to rest before the second move re-enters. Measured readouts: `point=60,120 moves=2 leaves=1` where `leaves=0` is required, and `point=200,120 moves=4 leaves=2` where `leaves=1` is required (the green run printed the expected pair). The component is unchanged since the probe's 07:13 green run and the runtime binding is the same `.node` from 2026-10-21, so the next step is to instrument the enter/leave pair with the payload's `hovered` flag and the runtime's own `getElementsAt` for a frame whose picture box tweens (the surface-origin probe also lays out on every move), then decide whether the component should ignore a leave whose next delivered move is inside the frame or whether the probe must re-read the pointer after the tween. This is a flake to make deterministic, not a claim the row's measured magnification is wrong — the row cites the green 54-check run. **Resolved 2026-10-24 — the counter, not the component.** The probe counted leaves **cumulatively**, and its own park can take a leave the measured pointer never made: a full live run's previous probe may leave the pointer over the frame's box, so the frame is entered at mount and left when the probe parks, and the resting check then read that leave. Reproduced deterministically by entering the frame before the park: `point=60,120 moves=3 leaves=1` against a required `leaves=0`, and green with the counter reset on the frame's own entry (`point=60,120 moves=3 leaves=0`) — the same run, one line apart. The view now resets `leaves` in `onMouseEnter`, the check reads `no leave arrived between the pointer reaching the frame and this read`, and `image-zoom.test.ts` gains `counts a leave from the pointer's own arrival` (measured failing without the reset with `to contain 'onMouseEnter={() => setLeaves(0)}'`). The paint checks were already the guard against a pointer the component really dropped (a collapsed picture fails `the magnified picture is larger than the frame`), so no component change is owed. `--only image-zoom-lifecycle` green twice on 0.11.0 here (54 checks, 5.9 s and 7.3 s); `apps/playground/README.md` §`image-zoom-lifecycle` states the per-arrival rule and the measured reproduction. Owner: playground (the probe was).

`[x]` `packages/media`: **a ratio-locked crop drag slid the whole hole instead of stopping at the frame** — `fitRatio` took the width its height implied and capped it against the **whole frame**, then clamped the origin to fit, so a drag that reached one edge moved the corner the reader was not dragging: measured, a 2:1 hole at `60, 40, 100 × 50` in a 240×160 frame, dragged past the bottom edge, reported `0, 40, 240 × 120` where the fixed `nw` corner belongs at `60, 40` — the picture jumped under the reader. The cap is now the room the anchored corner leaves in the direction the hole grows (`roomW`, `roomH * ratio`), so the same drag stops at `60, 40, 180 × 90` with the opposite corner still. `src/crop/logic.test.ts` gains `stops a locked drag at the frame, not by sliding the anchored corner` (the `se` drag past the bottom edge and the `nw` drag past the top, the second keeping `se` at `200, 150`) and `reshapes a stored hole inside a frame its origin leaves no room in` (a 4:1 hole at `76, 0, 24 × 24` moves to `4, 0, 96 × 24` instead of painting past a 100-wide frame), and `src/behaviour/crop-area.test.tsx` `stops a locked resize at the frame instead of sliding the crop` (the shipped handle, dragged 1000 points down, reports the one capped rectangle). Directions measured: without the room cap the unit case reads `{ x: 0, y: 100, width: 400, height: 200 }` and the window case `{ x: 0, y: 40, width: 240, height: 120 }`; without the inside clamp the shaped case reads `{ x: 76, y: 0, width: 96, height: 24 }`; with both, the two files are 48/48 and 10/10 and the package 191 unit / 27 behaviour cases green, `check-types` clean. - **B3 (new, 2026-10-23 02:0x; resolved 2026-10-23)** — **`master` carried the deletion of a module it still imported.**

  `packages/components/src/internal/typeahead.{ts,test.ts}` out of the index while the
  components workstream had already moved them to `packages/components/src/typeahead.ts`

  checkout of `master` cannot type-check the components package, although **the working

  **Resolved by `83b3dfe4`** ("feat(components): publish the type-ahead seam"): HEAD now

`[x]` `packages/components`: **a pointer effect reads a box the runtime will not refresh** — measured on 0.11.0 in the real renderer: a box moved 120px by a padding change delivered **no** `onLayout` at all (its own size did not change, and the runtime only reports a layout whose box it can see change), while the pointer payload moved from `50, 30` to `170, 150` for the same spot on the box — so the two are in the same **window** space and only one of them is fresh. `Magnetic` and `ImageZoom` both keep the box from their last `onLayout` and subtract a **fresh** pointer point from it, so after a layout the window moves without resizing them (a pane opening above, a resize that only shifts) the lean/pan is computed from the centre the surface *used* to have: a magnetic plate leans the wrong way, a zoom pans as if the pointer were somewhere else, until something resizes the element. **Resolved 2026-10-23** — the repair is a 1px origin probe (`internal/surface-box.tsx`): the surface toggles the probe's width on every pointer read, so the runtime lays it out again and reports the origin the surface has now; the box is that origin with the surface's own measured size, and both components derive the lean/pan during render rather than storing the pull, so the reading that asked for the fresh box corrects the paint without waiting for another move. Proof: `magnetic.test.tsx`'s `leans from the box the surface is in now, not the one it first reported` and `image-zoom.test.tsx`'s `pans from the frame the surface is in now, not the one it first reported` move each surface 120px by a padding change and read the frame after one pointer move on a paused clock.
